label: Person
name: Adeodato Giovanni Piazza
summary:
Adeodato Giovanni Piazza OCD (1884–1957) was an Italian Carmelite cardinal who served as Patriarch of Venice from 1935 to 1948 and then as Secretary of the Sacred Consistorial Congregation from 1948 to 1957 — one of the most powerful curial positions, responsible for overseeing the worldwide appointment of bishops. Born in Vigo di Cadore in the Dolomites, he entered the Discalced Carmelite order and rose through its ranks before being elevated to the episcopate.

As Patriarch of Venice, Piazza occupied one of the most prestigious sees in Italy — the patriarchate that would later be held by Angelo Roncalli (the future Pope John XXIII) and Giovanni Battista Montini (the future Paul VI). His leadership of Venice during the Second World War and its aftermath required both pastoral sensitivity and institutional resilience. His appointment to the Consistorial Congregation placed him among the most influential figures in the global Catholic Church, shaping episcopal appointments across every continent.

Piazza was created Cardinal in 1937 by Pope Pius XI. His curial career under Pius XII reflected the centralised model of Church governance that characterised the mid-twentieth century papacy. As a Carmelite, he brought the mystical and contemplative tradition of his order to his administrative roles, representing the devotional depth that distinguished many of Italy's greatest churchmen.
